facts.raw_span: A 40-year-old man presented with a painful nodule on the lower part of his right leg
the lesion had been stable in size and painless for 4 years but had enlarged and become tender over the past 6 months
an irregular, firm, erythematous, mobile, tender mass measuring 3.5 × 2.3 × 1.7 cm was noted just above the lateral malleolus of the right leg
No popliteal or inguinal lymphadenopathy was present
there were no other suspicious cutaneous lesions
Routine blood tests, including complete blood count, fasting blood sugar, liver and renal function tests, were within normal limits
Tests for hepatitis B surface antigen and HIV were negative
a lobulated, tan-gray, firm mass partly covered by skin, measuring 3.5 × 2.3 × 1.7 cm
nests and fascicles of spindle-shaped to epithelioid cells with pale eosinophilic cytoplasm, vesicular nuclei, and prominent nucleoli within a collagenous stroma
Mitotic figures, including atypical forms, measured 7–8 per 10 high-power fields
Immunohistochemical staining showed strong positivity for vimentin and focal positivity for Melan-A and HMB-45
The tumor cells were negative for S-100 protein, pancytokeratin, epithelial membrane antigen, and CD31

concepts.why: The presence of nests and fascicles of spindle-shaped to epithelioid cells with pale eosinophilic cytoplasm, vesicular nuclei, and prominent nucleoli within a collagenous stroma, along with high mitotic figures and specific immunohistochemical staining patterns, are characteristic of dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans.

The combination of spindle-shaped to epithelioid cells, high mitotic figures, and specific immunohistochemical staining patterns could also suggest plexiform fibrohistiocytic tumor, although the absence of certain features makes it less likely.

The presence of atypical cells, high mitotic figures, and specific immunohistochemical staining patterns could suggest atypical fibroxanthoma, but the clinical presentation and other features are not as typical for this diagnosis.

The presence of spindle-shaped to epithelioid cells and high mitotic figures could suggest malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumor, but the lack of specific nerve sheath differentiation and other features makes this diagnosis less likely.
The presence of spindle-shaped cells and high mitotic figures could suggest leiomyosarcoma, but the lack of specific smooth muscle differentiation and other features makes this diagnosis less likely.

rationales.F01: The presence of a painful nodule is a non-specific finding.
rationales.F02: The change in size and tenderness of the lesion over time suggests a growing tumor.
rationales.F03: The description of the mass is consistent with a soft tissue tumor.
rationales.F09: The histological features are consistent with a dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans.
rationales.F10: The high mitotic rate suggests a malignant tumor.
rationales.F11: The immunohistochemical staining pattern is consistent with a dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans.
rationales.F12: The absence of staining for certain markers helps to rule out other tumor types.
